A1.justification: Both PDFs present the same PrivaCI-Bench study. The main text, figures, tables and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching, including the renumbered prompt tables.

before.justification: v1 reports original legal-compliance and context-understanding evaluations, ablations, and human annotation assessments in Section 5, with additional results in Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds prompt-sensitivity experiments in Appendix C.3 and Tables 13–14.

M1.justification: The benchmark construction pipeline, auxiliary knowledge graphs, judgment modules and original prompt templates are unchanged. Appendix C.3 evaluates prompt variations without introducing a new proposed method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same HIPAA, GDPR, EU AI Act and ACLU legal-compliance coverage and the same contextual-integrity multiple-choice tasks. The new sensitivity experiments reuse three existing regulatory subsets.

E2.justification: The evaluated models and existing DP, CoT, RAG and ground-truth-assisted comparisons are retained. Appendix C.3 uses the already evaluated Qwen-2.5-7B-Instruct and GPT-4o-mini with DP and CoT.

E3.justification: Appendix C.3 adds an evaluation contrasting repeated prompts with varied prompts for two models across three regulatory subsets. This supplementary design changes the testing procedure; the original benchmark settings and metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds a focused robustness analysis of accuracy stability under repeated and modified DP/CoT prompts. The existing CI/regulation ablations in Figure 2 and synthetic-case analysis in Appendix C.2 are retained.

E5.justification: v1 specifies single-run model evaluation. v2 newly reports mean accuracy and standard deviation for three repeated runs and three varied prompts in Tables 13–14, explicitly describing extra experiments. This uncertainty reporting is limited to the supplementary two-model study; the original score tables are unchanged.

E6.justification: Tables 13–14 add supplementary accuracy results, including GPT-4o-mini GDPR CoT means of 55.94 for repeated prompts and 82.26 for varied prompts. Earlier numerical results are retained. Table 13 also prints an invalid accuracy of 389.83 ± 0.90 for Qwen's GDPR CoT result; its intended value cannot be established.

T1.justification: The contextual-integrity framework and knowledge-graph definitions are unchanged. Neither version adds formal propositions, proofs or derivations relative to the other.

C1.justification: The abstract, introductory contribution list and conclusion retain the same claims about benchmark coverage, auxiliary knowledge bases, EU AI Act evaluation, contextual understanding and remaining compliance difficulties.

C2.justification: New limitations explain that legal compliance is only a minimum privacy baseline and can miss cultural, ethical and personal expectations. The ethics section cautions against professional reliance on LLM judgments. Appendix C.3 additionally interprets prompt sensitivity as evidence that models favor different CoT styles.

D1.justification: v2 newly discloses parsing-error checks involving three authors and two law students, prior anonymization of source cases, and context-length considerations behind excluding few-shot demonstrations. These disclosures do not establish a changed underlying pipeline. Existing generation settings, hardware and code-access information are retained; the new varied prompts are not supplied.

R1.justification: The bibliography and related-work section are retained. The new limitations explicitly engage the already cited Shvartzshnaider and Duddu (2025), agreeing that legal statutes cannot capture all privacy norms and positioning legal evaluation as a minimum baseline.

P1.justification: v2 adds Limitations, Ethical Considerations, Acknowledgements and Appendix C.3, expands author contact information, identifies the corresponding author and corrects the case-study heading. The existing scientific narrative is largely unchanged.

P2.justification: Two sensitivity-result tables are added as Tables 13–14. The existing prompt tables become Tables 15–16, with associated layout and pagination adjustments. Both figures and the earlier tables retain their content and display structure.

improvement.justification: v2 improves scope transparency by distinguishing legal compliance from broader privacy norms and adds potentially useful uncertainty evidence. However, the new analysis contains the impossible accuracy in Table 13, claims standard deviations below 2.5 despite a 2.70 entry in Table 14, and contradicts the Limitations statement that prompt sensitivity was not assessed. These unresolved reporting problems undermine the added evidence enough that a reliable net quality improvement cannot be established.
